references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 0
references.quote: (a) Applicability. This section applies to temporary signs and banners as described below for yard signs, freestanding banners, feather signs, and wall banners that are visible from the public right-of-way. Temporary signs and banners internal to a site not intended to be visible from passing vehicles in the public right-of-way are not subject to the following regulations.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 2
references.quote: (1) Temporary Sign. A “temporary sign” is a sign typically made of lightweight or flimsy material that can be easily or quickly mounted or removed (such as cloth, canvas, vinyl, cardboard, wallboard, or other light temporary materials), with or without a structural frame, intended for a temporary period of display.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 3
references.quote: (2) Banner. A “banner” means any strip of cloth, bunting, plastic, paper, or similar material, attached to any structure or framing intended for a temporary period of display. This definition does not include flags, pennants, or streamers.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 4
references.quote: (c) Generally. Temporary signs and banners shall comply with standards in the tables below and in this section. No sign permit is required.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 5
references.quote: (d) Prohibited. Temporary signs and banners are not allowed in the public right-of-way or on accessory structures including poles outside the public right-of-way unless otherwise allowed by this chapter.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 6
references.quote: (e) Exempted Signs. Temporary signs and banners on property that has not established a principal building/land use, such as during a construction event, are exempt from the standards of this chapter until such time as a principal building/land use is established. Vacant land that is not transitioning or under construction to a primary use/building is subject to the standards of this chapter.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 10
references.quote: A yard sign is a temporary sign supported by the ground independent of any other structure.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 12
references.quote: A freestanding banner is a banner that is mounted in the ground, typically on poles detached from a building or wall.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 343
references.quote: 1. Number. Properties may have one sign for every 200 feet of street frontage with a maximum of two.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 344
references.quote: 2. Removal. Feather signs shall be replaced or removed if they deteriorate by becoming frayed, faded, torn, or shredded in any manner.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 345
references.quote: (h) Portable Message Center Signs. Portable message center signs are subject to the following standards:

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 346
references.quote: (1) Definition. A portable message center sign is a portable sign containing changeable copy.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 347
references.quote: (2) Until October 1, 2020, portable message center signs are permitted only in C-2, C-3, I-1, I-2, and for churches and schools in residential districts. After October 1, 2020, portable message center signs are prohibited in all districts and for all uses.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 348
references.quote: (3) Use of a portable message center sign requires a sign permit.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 349
references.quote: (4) Use of a portable message center sign is restricted to two events per year, 30 calendar days per event maximum, 30 calendar days between events, and a maximum of 60 calendar days per year.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 350
references.quote: (5) All parts of the sign containing copy and/or illumination are restricted to an area of 32 square feet.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 351
references.quote: (6) The sign shall not exceed a height of six feet.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 352
references.quote: (7) The sign must be set back a minimum of five feet from any property line.

references.label: TMC 18.10.170 block 353
references.quote: (8) Flashing lights are prohibited, and any illumination shall comply with the electrical and fire codes adopted in TMC Title 14 .
